title: Index color tRNS can be shorter than PLTE
summary: Each byte in tRNS gives the transparency of the corresponding palette index, with subsequent indices without entries defaulting to fully opaque.
detail: For example, when the table has four colors and tRNS has only one zero byte, only index 0 is fully transparent.
boundary: tRNS for grayscale and truecolor images represent specified transparent sample values, which are interpreted differently.
relevance: Distinguishing visible image lack of color from original index does not exist.
